subject: physics

verification.note: The mark split is invented and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: Satellites that go round the earth in a
north-south orbit, passing over the poles,
are called polar satellites. They move in a
low orbit, a few hundred kilometres up.
steps.why: The name is the orbit: geostationary satellites sit over the equator, polar satellites cross the poles.
common_mistakes: Confusing them with geostationary satellites, which stay over the equator.

recall.must_convey: That polar satellites move in a low north-south orbit passing over the poles.

steps.memory_tip: Polar = passes over the poles: a low orbit running north to south.

steps.label: Why they are used

lines.text: Low orbit, north-south, over the poles

lines: The earth turns beneath them, so a polar
satellite sees a different strip of ground on
every pass and can survey the WHOLE earth.
steps.why: A geostationary satellite always sees the same face of the earth; a polar one eventually sees all of it.
common_mistakes: Giving television relay as the use — that is what a geostationary satellite does.

recall.must_convey: That the earth turns beneath them so they can survey the whole earth strip by strip.

steps.memory_tip: The earth turns underneath it, so strip by strip it photographs the WHOLE surface — mapping and weather.
